comment: Curated inventory of documented V2 customer behaviors read by BehaviorInventorySource. Categories follow Requirements 16.2, 16.5-16.10 and 17.11 (telemetry, logging, profile, region, credential, endpoint, checksum, compression, native-image, module-path, service-default, retry, signer, streaming, paginators, waiters, presigners, event streams, high-level libraries). IDs are stable; add entries, never rename them. 'reference' names the V2 source or developer-guide topic that defines the behavior.

behaviors.surface: Standard retry strategy: retryable error classification, exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts and token-bucket throttling.
Adaptive retry strategy: client-side rate limiting driven by throttling responses.
Legacy retry mode selected by AWS_RETRY_MODE=legacy or profile retry_mode=legacy.
Retry mode and max attempts resolved from client builder, aws.retryMode/AWS_RETRY_MODE, profile retry_mode and defaults mode.
Endpoints resolved from the service endpoint ruleset using region, FIPS, dual-stack and service-specific parameters.
endpointOverride on the client builder and request override configuration replaces the resolved endpoint URI.

behaviors.reference: SdkSystemSetting AWS_ENDPOINT_URL; profile endpoint_url and services sections
behaviors.surface: Global and service-specific endpoint URLs from AWS_ENDPOINT_URL*, aws.endpointUrl* and profile endpoint_url settings, disabled by ignore_configured_endpoint_urls.
FIPS and dual-stack endpoint selection from builder, environment, system property and profile.
Flexible request checksums (CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME, SHA1, SHA256) computed WHEN_SUPPORTED or WHEN_REQUIRED, including trailing checksums for streaming bodies.
Response checksum validation WHEN_SUPPORTED or WHEN_REQUIRED, failing the call on mismatch.
Request compression (gzip) for operations with the requestCompression trait, honoring the minimum size threshold and disable settings.
Default credentials chain order: system properties, environment, web identity token, profile (including SSO, process and assume-role), container, instance profile.
Credential caching with asynchronous prefetch and stale-time refresh for expiring credentials.
EC2 instance metadata credentials using IMDSv2 tokens with IMDSv1 fallback controls and endpoint configuration.
Default region chain order: aws.region system property, AWS_REGION environment, profile region, instance metadata.
Shared config and credentials file locations, parsing, merging and profile selection from AWS_PROFILE/aws.profile.
Profile file suppliers that reload the shared files when they change.
Defaults mode (legacy, standard, in-region, cross-region, mobile, auto) resolved from builder, AWS_DEFAULTS_MODE and profile, selecting service defaults.
API call and attempt timeouts from client and request override configuration.
Lazy sync Iterable and async Publisher paginators, including flattened item iteration and token propagation.
Sync and async waiters with modeled acceptors, backoff, max attempts and wait timeout.
Service presigners producing time-limited presigned URLs and headers with SigV4 query signing.

behaviors.reference: Developer guide: event streams; core/aws-core eventstream
behaviors.surface: Event stream input and output operations with framing, per-event signing and response handlers.
Sync RequestBody and ResponseTransformer streaming, including reset/replay for retries and content length handling.
Async AsyncRequestBody and AsyncResponseTransformer streaming with reactive-streams backpressure and cancellation.
SigV4 and SigV4a request signing selected by auth scheme resolution, including payload signing and chunked encoding.
Bearer token auth for services that model httpBearerAuth, with token provider chains.
ExecutionInterceptor hook order and frequency, including classpath-registered global interceptors.
Per-call and per-attempt core metrics collected and delivered to configured MetricPublishers.
User-agent composition including SDK, OS, language, feature metadata and application ID.
X-Amzn-Trace-Id propagation from the Lambda environment or system property.
SLF4J logging with request IDs, wire logging under software.amazon.awssdk.request and redaction of sensitive data.
Default sync and async HTTP client discovery from system properties and the class path.
HTTP client proxy configuration from builders, JVM proxy system properties and HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY environment variables.
GraalVM native-image builds of SDK clients with shipped reflection and resource configuration.
SDK artifacts usable on the Java module path with stable module names.
DynamoDB Enhanced sync and async table, index, batch, transaction, pagination, extension and document behaviors.
Cancelling an enhanced async future, page subscription or item subscription cancels the in-flight DynamoDB request and stops fetching further pages.
A failed, retried or cancelled enhanced sync or async call releases every HTTP exchange it opened and leaves stored items unchanged when a conditional write fails.

Retryable transport, throttling and server faults are retried below the enhanced call with the client's retry strategy and retry-delay hints; exhausted retries, malformed responses, identity and endpoint failures surface as SdkClientException, and modeled service errors keep their exception type, through the sync and async clients alike.
Enhanced clients and tables are safe for concurrent use: overlapping writes, conditional (versioned) updates, atomic counters and paginated queries lose no update.
Every request the enhanced clients send identifies the DynamoDB Enhanced Client in the user agent (API name hll/ddb-enh).

An error response whose error code the service model does not define surfaces as the service's base exception (for example DynamoDbException or S3Exception) carrying the error code, message and HTTP status.
S3 Transfer Manager upload, download, directory, multipart, progress, cancellation, resume and failure-cleanup behaviors.
Cancelling a transfer's completion future, or closing the transfer manager, cancels the transfer's in-flight part, range and directory-item requests; a cancelled multipart upload is aborted.

A failed multipart upload or copy aborts its multipart upload and completes no object; a resumed upload whose source changed aborts the stale upload; a failing directory item is reported in failedTransfers while the other items complete.

Request failures are retried by the S3 client from replayable part bodies without double-counting progress, and otherwise fail the transfer with the modeled or client exception reported to transfer listeners; an object replaced during a multipart download fails it with a precondition failure.
One transfer manager is safe for overlapping transfers; part and directory-item concurrency are bounded by the configured limits independently of the executor.
Downloads of an object, or into a file, through a presigned GetObject URL request.

S3 requests name the bucket once: in the host of a virtual-hosted request, or as the first path segment of a path-style request; the {Bucket} label never also stays in the path of a virtual-hosted request.
Java-based multipart S3 async client for parallel uploads and downloads.
IAM policy builder construction, JSON reading and writing.
S3 event notification model JSON reading and writing.
SNS message parsing and signature verification.
